title: The heart, reviewed

segments.voice: Yesterday, the creed, and your line: six to believe. Six things past the eye, from the hadith of Jibril. What real question did you ask? Day one thousand four hundred sixteen.

At a checkup, the doctor does two things. She looks for what is working: heart rate, breath, strength. And she looks for what is wrong: a fever, a cough, a lump that shouldn't be there. Two lists on one clipboard. The middle of this year did the same thing with a different organ. One list was the stations, the good things a heart can grow into. The other was the diseases, the things that make a heart sick. Today, the heart again: both lists, and the one sentence that holds them together.
screen: `TWO LISTS ON ONE CLIPBOARD.` → `WHAT'S WORKING, WHAT'S WRONG.` → `THE SAME CHECKUP FOR THE HEART.`

segments.voice: First, the sentence. In Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase, the Prophet, peace be upon him, says there is a lump of flesh in the body: if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. And it is the heart. Everything the year taught about the inner life hangs on that. Second, the stations. The year walked them one by one: turning back in repentance, watchfulness, taking account of yourself before you are taken to account, not being owned by things, patience, gratitude, trust after effort, contentment, love, and the two wings of fear and hope, with sincerity of intention running through all of them. Third, the diseases. Arrogance, which a hadith in Sahih Muslim defines, in paraphrase, as rejecting the truth and looking down on people. Envy. Showing off. Anger. Greed. Backbiting. Lying. Heedlessness, the plain forgetting of Allah in the rush of the day. And despair, the closed door. Al-Ghazali's Revival, which the year opened, has one part on the things that destroy and one part on the things that save. Two lists, one clipboard. Fourth, where it leads. The Qur'an describes a day when wealth and sons are no help, except to the one who comes to Allah with a sound heart, in paraphrase. That is the point of the checkup. Not a perfect score on either list, but a heart brought back, again and again, toward sound.
screen: `IF THE HEART IS SOUND, ALL IS SOUND.` · `THE STATIONS: WHAT A HEART GROWS INTO.` · `THE DISEASES: WHAT MAKES IT SICK.` · `COME WITH A SOUND HEART.`

segments.voice: The practice: check your heart. Settle into the sit, and if you like, place a hand on your chest. Breathe. Ask one question from the first list: where did I show patience, or gratitude, this week? Let one moment come. Then one from the second list: where did envy, or anger, or showing off, slip in? Let one moment come, without arguing with it. No verdict, no score. If you pray, you can turn both moments over to Allah in your own words. Then just rest with the hand there. The bell holds the time.
The heart. Al-qalb, the lump of flesh the hadith says the whole body follows, checked for what it is growing and what is making it sick. Today's word.

Your line: check the heart. Tonight, before sleep, take ten seconds for the checkup: one thing that grew today, one thing that made it sick. Tomorrow, the manners, reviewed. Day one thousand four hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Muslims who follow the inward path read works such as al-Ghazali's Revival of the Religious Sciences, study the virtues and diseases of the heart with a teacher, and take account of themselves at the end of the day.
